profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer at The Walt Disney Studios
profile.geoLocationName: Los Angeles County, California, United States
profile.summary: My passion for programming began at the age of 9 when I was introduced to GW-BASIC. I enjoyed reading technical books and was introduced to C and Pascal by age 12. I wrote a simple bulletin boarding system using Telix’s scripting language and SYSOP’ed a BBS at the age of 13. At that time, I accepted a $1000 challenge to compromise a BBS based on the Wildcat software. I succeeded but was never rewarded. By 13, I learned enough of the 80x86 assembly language to reverse-engineer several video games, copy protection schemes, and trial software. I would share the exploits/cracks on various BBSes. I also enjoyed writing and sharing text file tutorials on various topics such as cracking, ANSI exploits, and trojans. In 2004, I founded a web-development / web-hosting company. In 2008, I began a competition with colleagues where each contestant writes a password protection program in C while attempting to crack each others’ programs using GDB. In 2009, I developed an algorithm/engine that allowed one to geocode a skewed, artistically rendered city map which was immediately filed for patent by my employer. In 2011, I built and launched a travel-oriented social networking site in 88 days. Google Ventures, Launchpad LA, 500 Startups, IdeaLab were some notable series A investors for this startup. In 2012, I developed and open-sourced the first Instagram follow bot for Linux/OSX platforms. In 2016, I published the first Linux (ELF) Assembly virus tutorial on my tech blog which has attracted a substantial following. In 2017 I developed and open-sourced a blockchain / cryptocurrency / wallet. I published blockchain tutorials and hosted several blockchain seminars. In 2018, I cocreated an Ethereum smart contract service which allows Solidity developers to automatically and reliably invoke their smart contracts based on events. In my spare time, I experiment with computer vision, microcontrollers, robots, and build/race FPV quadcopters. I seek to contribute and learn from others. Meanwhile, I continue this humble journey as a student and try my best to stay current with the industry.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
Help launch the Movies Anywhere service
Develop and maintain microservices using Java 8, Spring, Spring Boot 2, ActiveMQ, Maven, React, Redux, Kotlin
Perform a database migration from Oracle to Postgres with less than 10 minutes of downtime
Migrate cluster from the old data center to AWS with less than 30 minutes of downtime
Handle systems engineering responsibilities using various AWS services, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform
Maintain the CI/CD pipeline using Jenkins, Helm
Write unit tests, integration tests, end-to-end tests, performance tests
Build various performance tests (load tests, soak tests) using Jmeter/Blazemeter
Apply Extreme Programming practices, TDD, Pair Programming
Work with and receive coaching from Pivotal Labs
Switch teams and lead the Roku development team
Help develop the Movies Anywhere SmartTV application using Google Closure
Refactor and maintain the Roku Movies Anywhere Client using Brightscript and introduce unit tests to the codebase
Launch key features for Roku including: ScreenPass, WatchTogether (first Roku app to support a co-viewing experience)
